title: Philippine Inbound Remittance Operations
thesis: Snowflake turns daily corridor activity from a fictional Philippine remittance operator into straight-through and exception KPIs, 7-day failed-transfer risk scores, screening anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Straight-through rate, exceptions raised, failed transfers and PHP payout value for 40 corridors from Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, the United States, Hong Kong and Singapore into five Philippine payout cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it can be traced back to corridor-day rows.
The exception-type chart shows which exceptions end as failed transfers and which always clear, such as payout network outages.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of remittance KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which corridors should the exceptions team watch first?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each corridor's probability of a failed transfer in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent 14 days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags screening hit rate outliers per corridor, and the forecast projects operator-wide exception volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

talking_points: Prefunding reconciliation compliance with payout partners, payout-partner due-diligence coverage and pending documents frame the control gaps.
Reconciliation compliance against failed transfers by corridor shows where weak reconciliation and failures move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, corridor, exception-type and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a transfer drops into exception right now?

talking_points: Live transfer events land in RAW.LIVE_TRANSFERS, from the simulator or from Amazon Data Firehose through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs EXCEPTION events with an SOP hint and the corridor's current risk band, then emails the on-call remittance operations analyst.
tabs.call_out: From remittance exception to case in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over 14 synthetic remittance exception-handling SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (Data Firehose, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
